review_reference: Owner decision of 2026-11-10, relayed by Ola (clinical owner), for 0121 (Access PIN): "a PIN gives exactly 24 hours of read AND write access to all records, with no separate 'Ask for more access'", for the same staff roles as today; the backend goes live first, then the website. Numbered 0121, the next number after every migration on staging and on the open branches (0109-0120); the coordinator renumbers it at merge. Unsigned: reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs (the plain-English declaration for the owner is in the pull request).
evidence: Single migration 0121_patient_access_pin_day_read_write.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES: (a) access_requests_pin_scope_ck and consent_grants_pin_scope_ck (0033) allow scope read_records or write_records for a row whose authorization_method is patient_access_pin (still purpose direct-care and break_glass false); each dropped and added NOT VALID, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT. (b) CREATE OR REPLACE of identity.access_patient_with_pin(text,text,integer) from 0098's body (md5 830c1baa4bca3df57cc02b7b002a8831 before, e17e8bb85b755866bb0f1a03b5555c23 after): every grant lasts exactly 1440 minutes (24 hours), whatever duration is asked (owner decision of 2026-11-10); the argument requested_duration_minutes is kept, so old and new callers both work, and is still checked as 5-1440 (was 5-60), a missing or out-of-range value refused as before; the access request's requested_duration_minutes and the audit's duration_minutes say 1440, a replay's audit too (the reused grant keeps its own 24-hour expiry); the request and grant it inserts are write_records (was read_records); a still-valid PIN grant is reused only if write_records (an older read_records PIN grant is not reused and is left to run out); a deny directive stops it if its actions are empty or include read_records or write_records (was read_records only); the success and replay audit details and the PatientAccessPinVerified payload carry scope. Every other line is 0098's; signature, result, owner, plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path identity, auth, audit, platform, pg_temp and ACL (hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime EXECUTE) are unchanged and compared attribute by attribute after. (c) identity_outbox_minimum_necessary (0033) accepts a PatientAccessPinVerified payload of {consentGrantId, reviewRequired} or {consentGrantId, reviewRequired, scope} with scope read_records or write_records (EmergencyAccessActivated unchanged); dropped and added NOT VALID, then validated. (d) ALTER POLICY identity_outbox_patient_access_pin_insert (0033): the grant may be read_records or write_records and the payload's scope, when present, must be the grant's; name, command, permissive and roles unchanged. No table, column, index, trigger, role, permission or grant change; runtime-grants.sql unchanged; no row written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: identity-api reads the same result columns; today's image sends 15 or the caller's 5-60 and keeps working (the grant is then write_records for 24 hours, whatever it asks); the new identity-api (same pull request) asks for 1440 by default and accepts 5-1440, and the database always gives 1440. The event dispatcher and notification worker change that accepts both the two-key and the three-key PIN notice is a separate pull request (hid-system#206, branch claude/fervent-galileo-datz4t-pin-notice-scope, no migration) that must be merged and released before 0121 (release order: hid-system#206 first, then 0121 with identity-api, hid-system#208, renumbered at merge, then hid-system#207 and health#197): a release carrying a migration applies it before rolling out the services (scripts/production_deployment.py), and a PIN notice raised before the new services run would be refused by the old check and not retried. The websites (hid-system apps/web, hid-system#207, and health's staff site, health#197) keep working and change their words and duration after 0121 is live; until then a PIN used there gives write_records for 24 hours though the site asks 60 minutes and its words are out of date. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): the objects touched exist (else '0121: 0001-0108 must be applied first'); not applied yet (else '0121: already applied'); md5 of access_patient_with_pin (0098's), auth.account_id_for_subject, auth.membership_has_permission, the five platform session readers, identity.sealed_demo_facility and sealed_demo_patient, has_active_consent_grant (0104's) and records_processing_direct_care_cover (0108's); the function's attributes and result; the three CHECK constraints and the policy exactly as 0033 made them; consent_directive_versions.actions text[] NOT NULL; outbox_events forces row-level security; one owner for access_requests, consent_grants, outbox_events and the function, the applier it or a member with INHERIT and SET, holding USAGE and CREATE on schema identity. LOCKS: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.access_requests, identity.consent_grants and identity.outbox_events until commit (the runner applies the file in one transaction, so NOT VALID then VALIDATE does not shorten it); apply time 17-25 ms on the test databases; behind a session holding a lock on one of those tables the runner stops after its 5 s lock_timeout with nothing applied. PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (created and deleted): FRESH install of all 110 files (plan 110 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending), role bootstrap and verification pass, the file again answers '0121: already applied', all 81 database suites pass. UPGRADE from staging bf4ea233's 109 files and runtime-grants.sql: the updated PIN suite fails there; plan 1 pending (0121 with this sha256), dry run rolled back (body still 0098's), apply, 0 pending, the file again answers '0121: already applied'; 784 table and 588 function non-owner grants before, after and after a bootstrap; the PIN ACL unchanged; all 81 suites pass. SEEDED UPGRADE: a 60-minute read_records PIN grant and its two-key notice made by 0098's body before 0121 stay valid and untouched after it; the next correct PIN, asking 60 minutes, makes a new 24-hour write_records grant (existing_grant false, request 1440 minutes), the next, asking 5, replays it; the new notice carries scope write_records and the audit rows carry the scope and 1440 minutes. NOBYPASSRLS OWNER (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, owner and applier NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, applied by a member login; a stranger login refused): the PIN suite, its actor-window copy, sealed-demo-story, sealed-demo-tenant, patient-grant-revocation, records-processing, emergency-contacts and patient-sharing pass, so the function's outbox insert passes the changed policy under forced row-level security. MUTANTS (first round, on the earlier body): 13 of 13 fail the PIN suite (reuse lookup read_records, grant read_records, deny read only, deny write only, empty actions ignored, duration 60, duration 1441, no audit scope, no notice scope, policy without the payload check, either PIN constraint without the scope rule, the outbox minimum without the payload rule). EXACTLY 24 HOURS (2026-11-10): the new PIN suite cases (a call asking 60 and one asking 5 each get a 1440-minute write_records grant, the request stores 1440 and the audit says 1440; the replay asking 60 audits 1440; 4, 1441 and null refused) each fail on the previous body (6453e3e4c3906e4e565fa93c2979a865), checked one at a time. SUITE: services/ehr-api/database/tests/patient-access-pin.integration.sql (4, 1441 and null refused; 1440, 60 and 5 each give a write_records grant and request of exactly 24 hours, write allowed at its facility only; replay returns the same write grant; deny of writing, of every action, and of reading stop it, a deny for another purpose does not; an old read grant is not reused; audit and notice carry the scope; the constraints and outbox minimum refuse other scopes and shapes; the policy refuses a payload naming another scope). Also updated: patient-access-pin-actor-window, patient-grant-revocation, records-processing, sealed-demo-story (a PIN asking 30 minutes gives 24 hours) and sealed-demo-tenant (the PIN body's md5 pin, e17e8bb85b755866bb0f1a03b5555c23).
